classification.difficultyReason: Choose to differentiate, identify the actual reversal from the sign of velocity, and split the interval there before summing the absolute changes in position.

content.prompt:
A particle moves with displacement–time equation

$$x=2t^3-6t^2$$

By analysing the motion, find how far the particle travels in the first four seconds of motion.

answer.short:
$48\ \text{m}$.

Add the distances on either side of the direction change at $t=2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\frac{dx}{dt}\\v(t)&=6t^2-12t\\v(t)&=6t(t-2)\end{align*}$$

The particle moves left for $0<t<2$ and right for $2<t\le 4$, so it changes direction at $t=2$.

$$\begin{align*}x(0)&=0\\x(2)&=2(2)^3-6(2)^2=-8\\x(4)&=2(4)^3-6(4)^2=32\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance travelled}&=|-8-0|+|32-(-8)|\\\text{Distance travelled}&=8+40\\\text{Distance travelled}&=48\ \text{m}\end{align*}$$
